name: Hospitality & Event Management
notes: Knowledge areas come from the official FBLA 2025-26 Hospitality & Event Management guideline (updated January 2026), mirrored at https://www.pafbla.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Hospitality-and-Event-Management.pdf. The event is a role play (team of 1 to 3) with a 100-question, 50-minute objective test over 26 knowledge areas (A to Z). The subs here are a condensed 10-area grouping of those areas; lodging topics (hotel types, RevPAR, amenities, technology trends, tourism impact, the seven marketing functions) are filed under the closest sub. Questions are scenario-led and use U.S. conventions (GAAP for nonprofit donations, FLSA overtime, ADA access, USDA and FDA food safety, U.S. fire-code occupancy).

questions.q: A chapter has eight weeks to plan a 300-guest awards banquet. Which task should the event coordinator complete first?
choices: Set the event goals, budget and expected guest count
Book the keynote speaker before other dates fill up
Sign the caterer's contract to lock in menu pricing
Design the invitations so they can go out early
questions.explain: Goals, audience size and budget drive every later decision, including venue, catering and speaker choices, so they come before any booking or purchase.

questions.q: Which planning tool shows the sequence of dependent tasks and identifies the longest chain of tasks that sets the minimum time needed to finish the project?
choices: A Gantt chart with no dependency links
A critical path method (CPM) network
A work breakdown structure (WBS)
A responsibility (RACI) matrix
questions.explain: CPM links dependent tasks and finds the longest path, which sets the minimum duration; a WBS lists tasks without sequencing them, and a RACI matrix assigns roles.

questions.q: A run-of-show document is best described as:
choices: A summary of each vendor's contract terms, deposits and deadlines
A month-by-month planning calendar for the committee and its chairs
A minute-by-minute script of event-day cues, speakers and staff
A list of registered guests and their meal choices
questions.explain: The run-of-show is the operational script the team uses during the event itself.

questions.q: A planner learns that an outdoor reception has a 40 percent chance of rain. What is the most effective step?
choices: Wait for the forecast on the event morning, then decide
Move the event indoors now and release the outdoor site
Rent umbrellas for guests and keep only the outdoor plan
Hold an indoor backup space and set a firm decision deadline
questions.explain: A contingency plan with a backup space and a decision deadline protects the event without cancelling early on a forecast alone.

questions.q: Which objective is written as a SMART objective?
choices: Recruit 40 volunteers and raise $1,500 for the food bank by March 15
Recruit as many volunteers as possible for the food drive this spring
Raise more money for the food bank than the chapter did last year
Run a well-organized food drive that members will enjoy
questions.explain: SMART objectives are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. Only one choice names exact targets and a deadline; 'as many as possible' and 'more than last year' are not specific targets.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a floor plan in event planning?
choices: To list each vendor's arrival time and the load-in order at the dock
To show seating, stage, service and exit locations to scale
To show the order of speakers and cues on event day
To show which committee member owns each planning task and deadline
questions.explain: A scaled floor plan lets the planner check aisle widths, exits, sightlines and service routes, including fire-code clearances, before the event. Load-in order, cue order and task owners belong in other documents.

questions.q: A three-day conference expects a breakout room to exceed its capacity on day two. Which action best solves the problem while protecting the schedule?
choices: Keep the room as booked and let the extra attendees stand along the walls
Repeat the session on day three for anyone turned away
Move it to a larger room in the venue and update signs and the app
Cut the session time in half and run it twice in the same small room
questions.explain: Relocating within the venue and updating every channel fixes capacity without breaking the schedule or exceeding the room's occupancy load. Adding or splitting sessions changes the program.

questions.q: At a formal awards banquet, the chapter president hosts from the center seat of the head table. Under standard protocol, where does the guest of honor sit?
choices: At the end of the head table nearest the podium
At a reserved VIP table directly below the stage
At the president's immediate left
At the president's immediate right
questions.explain: The place of honor is to the host's right; the second-ranking guest usually sits to the host's left.

questions.q: Which planning tool shows each task as a bar on a calendar so the team can see start dates, durations and overlapping work?
choices: A Gantt chart
An organizational chart
A fishbone diagram
A SWOT matrix
questions.explain: A Gantt chart plots tasks as bars against a timeline; an org chart shows reporting lines, a fishbone diagram traces the causes of a problem, and SWOT is a situation analysis.

questions.q: A planner's schedule sets the final catering headcount for day 20, but the RSVP deadline is day 25. What is the best fix?
choices: Keep the order and add a large meal buffer for late replies
Move the RSVP deadline ahead of the catering count, with a buffer
Give the caterer the day-20 count and ignore later RSVPs
Push the catering count past the caterer's contract deadline to be safe
questions.explain: The headcount must be locked after RSVPs close; reversing the order creates an unplanned cost or waste.

questions.q: Which factor should be assessed first when selecting a venue for a 200-person conference?
choices: Its distance from the nearest airport and the main conference hotels
The in-house catering menu and its per-plate prices for each meal
Capacity for the planned layout, within the fire-code limit
The quality of its decor and natural lighting
questions.explain: Capacity and legal occupancy are non-negotiable, so they screen venues before any preference is considered.

questions.q: A banquet needs seating for 200 guests at round tables of 10. How many tables are needed?
questions.explain: 200 divided by 10 is 20. Dividing by 8 gives 25 and dividing by 12 gives about 17, which are the trap answers for other table sizes.

questions.q: A ballroom will host a 45-minute keynote with no meal and no need for writing surfaces. Which setup seats the most people in the room?
choices: Theater style
Banquet rounds
Classroom style
Hollow square
questions.explain: Theater style is rows of chairs with no tables, so it fits the most people for a presentation. Classroom style adds tables for note-taking, and banquet rounds are for meals.

questions.q: Before signing an outdoor venue contract, which question is most important to ask the site manager?
choices: How many staff will the venue provide for setup, service and final cleanup?
What are the rules on permits, noise limits and weather cancellation?
Which caterers and rental firms are on the venue's preferred vendor list?
How early can vendors arrive on event day for load-in?
questions.explain: Permits, noise rules and weather policy can cancel or disrupt an outdoor event, so they must be settled up front.

questions.q: At a conference, staff, speakers, exhibitors and attendees need access to different areas. Which tool best controls who enters each area?
choices: A seating chart for the general session
A printed agenda handed out at check-in
Color-coded badges tied to access zones
One wristband color for every guest
questions.explain: A credential system with badges coded by role lets door staff see at a glance who may enter each zone, such as backstage or the exhibit hall.

questions.q: A venue charges $3,000 for room rental, $25 per guest for 150 guests, and a $500 setup fee. What is the total venue cost?
questions.explain: 3,000 plus (25 times 150 = 3,750) plus 500 equals 7,250. Forgetting the setup fee gives $6,750.

questions.q: Which layout decision best supports smooth guest flow at registration?
choices: Check-in at the main entrance, with signs and extra lanes at peak
Check-in inside the main hall so guests are counted as they sit
One central check-in table, staffed by the event chair
Check-in at the coat check so guests make only one stop
questions.explain: Registration at the entrance with clear signage and extra lanes prevents bottlenecks at peak arrival times.

questions.q: A venue contract includes a minimum food and beverage spend of $4,000, but projected catering spend is $2,800. What is the best action?
choices: Sign as written and treat the minimum as an estimate
Negotiate a lower minimum or plan added items, in writing
Sign now and ask the venue to waive the shortfall later
Cut the guest count so the per-guest spend looks higher
questions.explain: Minimum spend clauses are negotiable, and the shortfall is a real cost that must be resolved before the contract is signed.

questions.q: In U.S. event planning, what does ADA compliance require of a venue layout?
choices: A separate accessible entrance used only by wheelchair users
Accessible features only in buildings constructed after the ADA was passed in 1990
Accessible routes, entrances and restrooms for people with disabilities
Elevators in every building, regardless of the number of floors
questions.explain: Title III of the ADA requires public accommodations, including event venues, to provide accessible routes, entrances and facilities. Existing buildings are covered too: they must remove barriers where that is readily achievable.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a site inspection before a major event?
choices: To sign the contract and pay the deposit in person with the manager
To taste the menu options with the chef and choose the plated dinner
To photograph the venue for the event's marketing
To check sightlines, power, load-in and exits against the plan
questions.explain: A site visit verifies that the plan works in the actual space, catching problems before they become day-of failures.

questions.q: What is a budget variance?
choices: The difference between budgeted and actual amounts for a line item
The share of the total budget assigned to a single line item
The amount held back to cover unexpected event costs
The change in ticket price between the early-bird and regular sales periods
questions.explain: A variance measures how far actual results are from the budget, favorable or unfavorable.

questions.q: Which of these is a fixed cost for a conference?
choices: A per-plate charge for each guest's meal
A flat venue rental fee, whatever the turnout
A printed name badge made for each guest
A commission paid on each sponsorship sold
questions.explain: Fixed costs do not change with attendance; per-guest and commission costs are variable.

questions.q: A chapter sells 120 tickets at $25 each and has $2,400 in total expenses. What is the net profit?
questions.explain: Revenue is 120 times 25, which is 3,000. Subtracting expenses of 2,400 leaves 600.

questions.q: A 200-room hotel sold 150 rooms last night at an average daily rate (ADR) of $120. What was its revenue per available room (RevPAR)?
questions.explain: RevPAR is room revenue divided by rooms available: 150 times $120 is $18,000, and $18,000 divided by 200 is $90. It also equals occupancy (75 percent) times ADR. $120 is the ADR itself.

questions.q: Fixed costs are $1,800, the ticket price is $30, and variable cost is $12 per guest. What is the break-even attendance?
questions.explain: The contribution margin is 30 minus 12, which is 18. Then 1,800 divided by 18 equals 100 guests.

questions.q: What is a contingency reserve in an event budget?
choices: Funds committed to the largest single expense, such as the venue
Money set aside, as a share of the budget, for unexpected costs
Sponsor money that must be spent in full before the event takes place
Profit left over after the event that goes to the chapter
questions.explain: The reserve absorbs surprises such as price increases or weather costs without breaking the budget.

questions.q: A sponsor donates $1,000 of printed banners instead of cash. How should the chapter record the donation?
choices: At zero, since no cash changed hands with the sponsor
Only in a footnote, since goods are not counted as revenue
As in-kind revenue at fair value, with a matching expense
As a liability, since the chapter owes the sponsor publicity
questions.explain: Under U.S. GAAP for nonprofits (ASC 958), contributed goods are recorded as contribution revenue at fair value, with an expense recognized when they are used.

questions.q: Which is the best way to control spending during an event?
choices: Give each committee a lump sum and reconcile all the receipts after the event
Have the treasurer approve only those purchases that cost more than $1,000
Review the full budget once, a week before the event
Track spending against each budget line and approve changes in writing
questions.explain: Daily tracking against budget lines catches overruns while there is still time to correct them.

questions.q: A food budget is $900 for 150 guests. The caterer quotes $8.50 per guest. What is the result?
choices: $1,275, over budget
$900, within budget
$1,275, within budget
$1,175, over budget
questions.explain: 150 times $8.50 equals $1,275, which is $375 over the $900 budget.

questions.q: Which statement about accrual and cash accounting for an event is correct?
choices: Cash basis records revenue when it is earned, whenever payment arrives
Accrual basis records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred
Accrual basis records revenue only when the cash is deposited
Cash basis is the method U.S. GAAP requires for financial statements
questions.explain: Accrual accounting matches income and costs to the period they relate to, which is why it is preferred for multi-period comparison.

questions.q: Which document defines the scope, price and responsibilities between an event planner and a caterer?
choices: A run-of-show script
A request for proposal (RFP)
A signed contract or letter of agreement
A final itemized invoice from the caterer
questions.explain: A signed agreement sets what is delivered, when, at what price, and who is responsible if something goes wrong.

questions.q: A vendor contract includes a force majeure clause. What does it address?
choices: Penalties the client owes for paying a vendor's invoice after the due date
Refunds owed to guests who cannot attend the event
Damages owed when one party cancels the contract for its own convenience
Events beyond either party's control that may excuse performance
questions.explain: Force majeure clauses allocate risk for events outside the parties' control; their scope depends on the exact wording.

questions.q: Which is the strongest reason to get three bids before hiring an audio-visual vendor?
choices: It lets the chapter compare price, scope and references side by side
Vendors are required to lower their prices once they know they are competing
It replaces the need for a signed contract with the winner
It obliges each bidder to hold its price for the full year
questions.explain: Comparing scope and references matters as much as price; the cheapest bid is not always the best value.

questions.q: What is a deposit in a vendor agreement?
choices: The final balance owed to the vendor once the event is over
A partial upfront payment that secures the date or service
A fee charged only if the client cancels late
A gratuity added to the bill for service staff
questions.explain: Deposits reserve the vendor's time; the refund terms should be spelled out in the contract.

questions.q: A caterer requires a final guest count seven days before the event, and later changes are billed at 100 percent of the per-plate price. RSVPs are still changing. What is the best action?
choices: Give the lowest RSVP count and add guests later as needed
Wait until the event day and pay only for the number of guests actually served
Confirm a count with a small buffer and get the change policy in writing
Give the highest possible count so that no guest could ever go without a meal
questions.explain: Locking a count with a buffer, while knowing the cost of changes, avoids paying for unused meals without risking shortages.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a certificate of insurance requested from a vendor?
choices: To show the vendor holds the business license that the city requires
To prove the vendor's equipment is new and under warranty
To confirm the vendor's prices include all taxes and fees
To verify the vendor carries liability insurance at stated limits
questions.explain: A certificate shows the vendor's coverage limits and names the chapter as additional insured if the contract requires it.

questions.q: Which term describes an outside business that supplies services under a written agreement with defined deliverables, rather than working as an employee?
choices: Independent contractor
Temporary employee
Event sponsor
Volunteer
questions.explain: A contractor delivers defined services for a fee; the contract, not the relationship, defines the obligations.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a verbal agreement for a one-day event service?
choices: Verbal agreements are never legally enforceable
They can be enforceable, but written terms are easier to prove
They become enforceable only once a notary or lawyer witnesses them
They are enforceable only for deals worth less than $500 in total
questions.explain: Oral contracts for services are generally enforceable. The statute of frauds requires a writing only for certain deals, such as UCC sales of goods of $500 or more or contracts that cannot be performed within a year; the practical problem is proving the terms.

questions.q: Which practice best protects a chapter when a vendor fails to deliver a rented sound system?
choices: Pay the full balance anyway to keep a good working relationship
Accept any substitute system the vendor sends, without comment
Enforce the contract's remedy terms and document the failure
Post a public online review before contacting the vendor at all
questions.explain: Written documentation and the contract's remedy clause are what support a refund or credit claim.

questions.q: A venue contract says cancelling within 60 days of the event costs 50 percent of the rental fee, and within 14 days costs 100 percent. The chapter cancels 30 days before the event. What must it pay?
choices: Nothing, since it cancelled more than 14 days out
100 percent of the rental fee
75 percent of the rental fee
50 percent of the rental fee
questions.explain: Thirty days out is inside the 60-day window but outside the 14-day window, so the 50 percent tier applies.

questions.q: Which promotion method is most effective for a small chapter's bake sale at low cost?
choices: Social posts, school announcements and posters in busy hallways
A paid ad in the local newspaper's weekend edition
A direct-mail postcard sent to every household in the surrounding area
A sponsored spot on a regional radio station
questions.explain: Free and targeted channels reach the chapter's real audience at minimal cost.

questions.q: What is a target audience?
choices: Everyone in the community who could possibly be interested in attending
The specific group the event is designed for and likely to attract
The businesses that pay to sponsor, exhibit or advertise at the event
The guests who attended the same event last year
questions.explain: Targeting narrows messaging, channel choice and pricing to the people most likely to say yes.

questions.q: A resort gathers guest surveys, booking data and competitors' rates and stores them for managers to use in decisions. Which of the seven marketing functions is this?
choices: Product/service management
Distribution
Marketing-information management
Promotion
questions.explain: Gathering, storing and analyzing data for decisions is marketing-information management; product/service management is what managers then decide to offer using that data.

questions.q: Which metric best measures the reach of a social media campaign?
choices: Click-through rate on the event link
Number of comments and shares
Registrations that came from the tracked link
Impressions and unique accounts reached
questions.explain: Reach measures how many people saw the content; engagement and conversion are separate metrics.

questions.q: Which content is most effective for a promotional flyer?
choices: Event name, date, time, place and a clear call to action
A detailed history of the chapter and its past events
A full list of every vendor and sponsor involved
A large photo, with event details left for the website
questions.explain: A flyer must answer the basic questions in seconds because it is read briefly.

questions.q: Last month 50 of 1,000 website visitors registered. This month 80 of 1,200 registered. What happened to the registration rate?
choices: It fell from 6.7 to 5.0 percent
It rose from 5.0 to 6.7 percent
It stayed at 5.0 percent both months
It rose from 5.0 to 8.0 percent
questions.explain: Conversion is registrations divided by visitors: 50/1,000 is 5.0 percent and 80/1,200 is 6.7 percent.

questions.q: Which approach best uses sponsorship benefits to attract sponsors?
choices: Free admission for the sponsor, with no other benefits
A thank-you letter after the event instead of public credit
Tiered packages with defined benefits such as logo placement
One flat price for every sponsor, with benefits set later
questions.explain: Sponsors buy defined, measurable exposure; vague promises rarely close.

questions.q: What is a call to action in promotional material?
choices: The memorable slogan that sums up the event
The sponsor's logo shown with its tagline
The headline that names the event, its date and its venue
An instruction to act, such as 'Register by May 1'
questions.explain: A call to action converts interest into behavior, such as registering or buying a ticket.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of early-bird ticket pricing?
choices: It drives early commitments and gives an early head count
It lowers the event's fixed costs, such as the venue fee
It raises the average ticket price paid per guest
It guarantees sponsors will sign on sooner
questions.explain: Early sales improve planning accuracy and cash flow, though they reduce average ticket revenue.

questions.q: A chapter wants to know whether its Instagram promotion drove the event. Which pair of metrics best shows impact on the event itself?
choices: Likes and follower growth on the account during the campaign
Tracked-link registrations and check-in attendance
Shares and saves on each promotional post
Impressions and the comment count on each promotional post
questions.explain: Impressions and comments measure the post; only tracked registrations and check-ins measure the event outcome.

questions.q: Which hotel technology trend lets a guest skip the front desk entirely on arrival?
choices: A property management system that tracks room status
A central reservation system linked to travel sites
Mobile check-in with a digital key on the guest's phone
A revenue management system that adjusts room rates
questions.explain: Mobile check-in plus a phone-based digital key lets guests go straight to the room; the other systems run behind the scenes and do not change the arrival process.

questions.q: A guest with a severe food allergy is seated where the meal contains the allergen. What is the best first step?
choices: Serve the meal and ask the guest to pick around the allergen
Assume the guest will avoid the dish, since they listed the allergy on the RSVP
Offer the guest the vegetarian plate already on the menu
Alert the kitchen and servers, and confirm a safe meal before serving
questions.explain: Allergy safety comes first: the kitchen must confirm an allergen-free meal, since a substitute plate may still contain the allergen.

questions.q: What does service recovery mean?
choices: Restoring a guest's trust after a service failure with an apology and a fix
Cutting service staff hours after a slow season to recover the lost labor costs
Collecting unpaid balances from guests after they check out
Restoring service after a power outage or system failure
questions.explain: Good recovery turns a failure into a retained guest, often more loyal than before.

questions.q: Which is an example of a guest touchpoint?
choices: An entry in the event's accounting ledger
The registration desk, event app or follow-up email
A vendor invoice approved by the treasurer
A staff schedule posted on the wall of the back office
questions.explain: A touchpoint is any moment a guest interacts with the event, which is where the experience is shaped.

questions.q: A conference survey averages 4.6 out of 5, but 30 percent of attendees skipped the food question. What is the most accurate interpretation?
choices: Food scored well, since the overall average across all items was 4.6
Food was clearly the weakest part of the event
Skipped answers may hide a food problem worth a follow-up question
The survey is now invalid, so all of its results should be thrown out
questions.explain: High averages can mask gaps; nonresponse on a topic is a signal worth investigating.

questions.q: A guest complains about a long line at registration. Which response is best?
choices: Apologize, and reassure the guest that the line will start moving soon
Explain politely that long lines are normal at large, well-attended events
Offer a free drink ticket and return to other duties
Acknowledge the wait, give a time estimate and open another lane
questions.explain: Acknowledging the problem and offering a concrete fix changes the guest's experience immediately.

questions.q: Which feature most clearly separates a full-service hotel from a limited-service hotel?
choices: On-site restaurants, room service and banquet space
A front desk staffed 24 hours a day
Free Wi-Fi and a complimentary breakfast
Rooms with private bathrooms and daily housekeeping service
questions.explain: Limited-service hotels often offer a 24-hour desk, free breakfast and Wi-Fi; a full-service hotel adds food and beverage outlets, room service and meeting or banquet space.

questions.q: A hotel guest reports noise from a nearby ballroom event. Which response reflects good hospitality practice?
choices: Apologize and say the event will end at its scheduled time
Offer a room change and log the issue so the event team can act
Offer a discount at checkout if the guest still complains then
Ask the guest to call hotel security directly about the noise
questions.explain: Solving the guest's problem and passing the root cause to the event team is standard hospitality practice.

questions.q: In the gaps model of service quality (SERVQUAL), what does the customer gap measure?
choices: The difference between a service's cost and its price
The difference between what managers think guests want and what they want
The difference between what guests expect and what they perceive they got
The difference between service standards and the service delivered
questions.explain: The customer gap is guest expectations versus guest perceptions. Manager beliefs versus real guest wants is the knowledge gap, and standards versus delivery is the performance gap.

questions.q: Which of these is a property-wide amenity rather than an in-room amenity?
choices: A minibar stocked with snacks
A coffee maker and kettle
A safe for guests' valuables
A fitness room and pool
questions.explain: Property-wide amenities are shared spaces and services such as a pool, fitness room or business lounge; minibars, coffee makers and room safes are in-room amenities.

questions.q: What does FIFO mean in food storage?
choices: First in, first out: older stock is used before newer stock
Freshest in front: newest stock goes where it is used first
Fresh in, frozen out: fresh items are used before frozen ones
Follow the invoice order: stock is counted by delivery date
questions.explain: FIFO reduces spoilage by rotating stock so older items are used first.

questions.q: According to USDA food-safety guidance, what is the temperature danger zone?
choices: 0 to 32 degrees F (about -18 to 0 C)
40 to 140 degrees F (about 4 to 60 C)
140 to 165 degrees F (about 60 to 74 C)
32 to 40 degrees F (about 0 to 4 C)
questions.explain: USDA says bacteria grow fastest between 40 and 140 degrees F. The FDA Food Code that inspectors enforce uses 41 and 135 degrees F as the cold- and hot-holding limits, so keep cold food at 41 or below and hot food at 135 or above.

questions.q: A caterer expects 1.1 buffet plates per guest for 150 guests. How many plates should be prepared?
questions.explain: 150 times 1.1 is 165. Dividing instead (150 / 1.1) gives about 137, a common slip.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a HACCP plan?
choices: To set menu prices based on the target food cost percentage
To schedule kitchen staff so each station is covered
To post health inspection scores for the public
To control food hazards at critical control points
questions.explain: HACCP is a systematic food-safety method built around critical control points.

questions.q: What is a standard recipe used for in event catering?
choices: Consistent quality, portions and per-guest cost
Setting the price of the venue rental
Planning the order in which the courses will be served
Scheduling when each cook starts a shift
questions.explain: A standard recipe lets the caterer predict cost and quality per guest, the basis for accurate quotes.

questions.q: A plated dinner has $18 of food cost per guest, and the target food cost percentage is 30 percent. What menu price per guest meets the target?
questions.explain: Food cost percentage is food cost divided by price, so price is $18 divided by 0.30, which is $60. Multiplying by 1.3 ($23.40) is the common error.

questions.q: Which beverage practice most reduces liability when alcohol is served at an event?
choices: Offering an open bar so guests do not crowd a slower cash bar line
Letting guests pour their own drinks at a self-serve station all night
Checking IDs and using licensed bartenders under a proper permit
Serving drinks only after the meal has been cleared
questions.explain: Hosts and licensees can be held liable for serving minors or visibly intoxicated guests under state dram shop and social host laws, so licensing, ID checks and trained servers reduce that risk.

questions.q: In banquet pricing, what is a cover?
choices: A fee for linens and table settings
A deposit that holds the reservation
The sales tax added to the food bill
One guest or place setting served a meal
questions.explain: Per-cover pricing charges by the number of guests served, not by the number of dishes.

questions.q: Which is the best way to reduce food waste after a buffet?
choices: Forecast counts from RSVPs and refill smaller batches
Set out all the food at once so the buffet looks full
Order extra so no dish ever runs out during service
Discard leftovers quickly without recording amounts
questions.explain: Good forecasting and refill planning cut waste while keeping the buffet full.

questions.q: A food truck arrives with a permit that expired two days before the event. What should the planner do first?
choices: Let the truck operate and ask for the renewed permit later
Require a current permit before the truck may serve
Assume the health department renewed it automatically
Charge the truck a late fee and let it serve as planned
questions.explain: Operating without a valid permit creates legal and health exposure for the host, so verification comes first.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a risk assessment in event planning?
choices: To set ticket prices high enough to cover the cost of event insurance
To list the staff who will work each event shift
To identify hazards, rate likelihood and impact, and plan controls
To record incidents after they happen so insurers can process claims
questions.explain: A risk assessment ranks hazards so the most serious ones get the most planning effort.

questions.q: Which insurance covers a claim that a guest was injured at an event because of the organizer's negligence?
choices: Commercial auto insurance
Workers' compensation insurance
Business interruption insurance
General liability insurance
questions.explain: General liability covers third-party bodily injury and property damage claims arising from the organizer's operations.

questions.q: What is an incident report used for?
choices: Documenting injuries, damage or unsafe conditions for follow-up
Rating each vendor's performance after the event
Recording guest complaints for the marketing team
Listing likely hazards and planned controls before the event begins
questions.explain: Prompt, factual incident reports support insurance claims and prevent repeat hazards.

questions.q: The fire marshal sets the room's occupancy at 400, but the chapter sells 450 tickets. What is the correct response?
choices: Sell all 450, since some ticket holders will not show up
Cap sales at the lawful limit and plan for overflow or refunds
Add standing room along the walls for the extra 50 guests
Ask the fire marshal to approve the extra 50 guests on the event day
questions.explain: Exceeding occupancy is a life-safety violation; the lawful limit governs sales.

questions.q: A chapter hires a DJ who is paid in cash under no contract, and the DJ is later injured on site. Which risk is most significant?
choices: Losing the chapter's sales tax exemption for the event
Paying the DJ more than the market rate
Unclear liability and workers' compensation exposure
Copyright claims over the songs the DJ played during the event
questions.explain: Without a contract or proper classification, responsibility for an injury is disputed and costly.

questions.q: What is the first priority in an emergency at an event?
choices: Secure the cash box and all of the ticket revenue first
Notify the event sponsors and the local media right away
Keep the program running on schedule so guests do not panic
Protect life safety: follow the plan and call 911
questions.explain: Life safety comes first; the emergency plan defines who calls for help and who directs guests.

questions.q: Which license allows copyrighted music to be played at a public event?
choices: A public performance license from ASCAP, BMI or SESAC
A synchronization license from the record label that owns the songs
A trademark license from each recording artist
A sales tax permit from the state revenue agency
questions.explain: Public performance of copyrighted music needs permission, typically a license from performing rights organizations such as ASCAP, BMI or SESAC. A sync license covers pairing music with video.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a waiver or release form for event participants?
choices: To guarantee that the participant will attend the event as registered
To record acceptance of known risks, which may limit some claims
To fully replace the chapter's need for general liability insurance
To protect the organizer in every case, even against gross negligence
questions.explain: A waiver can limit some claims, but it does not replace insurance, and courts generally will not enforce one against gross negligence.

questions.q: Which action best protects a chapter from volunteer injury claims?
choices: Have volunteers sign a waiver and skip other steps
Classify volunteers as contractors so they carry their own risk
Confirm accident or liability coverage and train before setup
Limit volunteers to tasks that take under two hours
questions.explain: Coverage and training reduce both the risk and the chapter's exposure if an injury occurs.

questions.q: A severe storm warning is issued two hours before an outdoor event. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Hold the event as planned and have a staff member watch the radar closely
Tell guests to bring umbrellas and rain jackets
Let each vendor decide on its own whether to stay open or pack up
Follow the weather plan: notify everyone, then move or postpone
questions.explain: A pre-agreed trigger and communication plan avoids panic decisions in the final hours.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a volunteer job description?
choices: To define duties, time commitment and expectations for each role
To record the hours each volunteer works for school service-hour credit
To recognize volunteers publicly after the event
To screen volunteers with a background check
questions.explain: Clear role descriptions reduce confusion and make accountability possible.

questions.q: Three committee chairs are not communicating. Which leadership approach is best?
choices: Let the chairs compete for a month and give the lead role to the best
Set regular check-ins, a shared timeline and clear decision rights
Remove the chair who communicates least from the team
Take over all three committee areas personally until the event ends
questions.explain: Structure and clear authority fix coordination failures without removing people or creating a bottleneck.

questions.q: What is a shift schedule used for during an event?
choices: Recording what each vendor is owed after the event
Listing the program's speakers and their cue times on the stage
Assigning staff to times and locations so coverage is clear
Tracking how many guests arrive in each time slot at the check-in desk
questions.explain: Shift schedules guarantee coverage at every station and make absences visible quickly.

questions.q: Which method is best for training event staff quickly?
choices: Email a detailed staff manual the night before
Train only the supervisors and let them coach their teams on the job
Have new staff shadow veterans during the event
Brief staff with a run-of-show walkthrough and a practice run
questions.explain: A walkthrough and practice build familiarity fast, and role cards keep staff focused on their own tasks.

questions.q: Under the U.S. Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), which worker is entitled to overtime pay?
choices: A non-exempt hourly employee who works 45 hours in a week
A volunteer who works 45 hours in a week for a nonprofit
A salaried exempt manager who works 45 hours in a week
An independent contractor who works 45 hours on a project
questions.explain: Non-exempt employees must receive time-and-a-half for hours over 40 in a workweek. Exempt salaried managers, true volunteers and independent contractors are not covered by that rule.

questions.q: Which statement about nonprofit volunteers is most accurate?
choices: Volunteers must be paid at least the minimum wage
Volunteers are unpaid but still need training and clear roles
Volunteers may not be reimbursed for any expenses they pay for
Volunteers must be added to the payroll as employees
questions.explain: Volunteer status does not remove the duty to keep volunteers safe and informed.

questions.q: What does a volunteer sign-in sheet support?
choices: Setting vendor payment amounts
Counting the tickets sold at the door that day
Accountability and an emergency headcount
Recognizing sponsors on event day
questions.explain: Sign-in records support accountability and a reliable headcount if an evacuation is needed.

questions.q: A staff member with a personal stake in one caterer is assigned to choose the caterer. What is the best action?
choices: Let the staff member choose, since they know the caterer well
Keep the conflict private to avoid embarrassing anyone
Pick the caterer on lowest price alone to avoid any bias
Disclose the conflict and have someone else decide
questions.explain: A conflict of interest must be disclosed and managed by reassigning the decision.

questions.q: Which leadership style fits a new volunteer team that needs clear direction?
choices: Directive at first, becoming more supportive as skills grow
Laissez-faire, letting the new team set its own direction from day one
Delegating, giving full authority to each member
Democratic, voting as a group on every task
questions.explain: Teams that are new need direction first; autonomy is earned as competence develops.

questions.q: A volunteer is consistently late for shifts. Which response is most constructive?
choices: Remove the volunteer from the schedule without discussion
Talk privately, restate expectations and agree on a plan
Overlook it, since volunteers are unpaid
Raise the problem with the whole team at the next full meeting
questions.explain: A private, documented conversation addresses the problem fairly and creates a record if the issue continues.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a post-event debrief?
choices: To approve final payments to every vendor
To thank sponsors and pitch next year's packages
To review results against goals and record lessons
To collect photos for the chapter's social media
questions.explain: A debrief turns one event's experience into improvements for the next.

questions.q: A chapter's goal was 200 attendees and 180 attended. What is the attainment rate?
choices: 80 percent
111 percent
95 percent
90 percent
questions.explain: Attainment is actual divided by goal: 180 divided by 200 is 0.90, or 90 percent. Dividing the other way gives about 111 percent.

questions.q: How is cost per attendee calculated?
choices: Total event cost divided by the number of attendees
Total revenue divided by the number of sponsors
Ticket price multiplied by the number of attendees
Venue capacity divided by the number of attendees
questions.explain: Cost per attendee shows the efficiency of spending and is useful for comparing events.

questions.q: Which metric best evaluates whether a change to the registration process succeeded?
choices: Number of event T-shirts sold at check-in
Registration completion rate and time to confirm a ticket
Growth in the chapter's social media followers since the change
Total revenue from all ticket types combined for the whole event
questions.explain: Process changes should be judged on the process outcome, such as completion rate and time to confirm.

questions.q: A city studies a convention's economic impact. Delegates spend money at hotels, and hotel workers then spend their wages at local shops. What is this chain of spending called?
choices: The substitution effect
The crowding-out effect
The multiplier effect
The halo effect
questions.explain: Tourism dollars ripple through the economy: direct spending creates indirect and induced spending, which is the multiplier effect.

questions.q: Which data point best evaluates the financial result of a fundraising event?
choices: Gross ticket sales and donation receipts for the night
Number of donors who gave
Average gift size per donor
Net proceeds after all costs, compared with budget
questions.explain: Net proceeds after costs are the financial result; gross receipts alone overstate the success.

questions.q: A hotel spent $5,000 on a booth at a bridal show. Weddings booked from the show produced $8,000 in gross profit. What was the return on investment?
choices: 60 percent
160 percent
37.5 percent
62.5 percent
questions.explain: ROI is (gain minus cost) divided by cost: ($8,000 minus $5,000) divided by $5,000 is 0.60, or 60 percent. 160 percent forgets to subtract the cost.

questions.q: Of 200 attendees, 60 returned the survey, and 70 percent of those rated the venue good or better. What is the most important caution?
choices: The 70 percent figure can safely be applied to all 200 attendees
A 30 percent response rate may not represent all attendees
The survey has too few questions to be useful
The venue rating should come from staff instead
questions.explain: Only 30 percent responded, so non-responders may differ; the result is informative but not conclusive.

questions.q: How should lessons learned from a debrief be used?
choices: Filed in the chapter archive for reference at a future date
Shared in a thank-you email to volunteers
Built into templates, timelines and vendor checklists
Presented to sponsors as part of the final event report
questions.explain: Lessons only matter when they change the templates and checklists the team actually uses.

questions.q: Projected net income was $4,000 ($13,000 revenue minus $9,000 expenses). Actual revenue was $12,000 and actual expenses were $10,000. What is the variance on net income?
choices: $2,000 favorable
$1,000 unfavorable
$6,000 favorable
$2,000 unfavorable
questions.explain: Actual net income is $2,000 against a $4,000 budget, a $2,000 unfavorable variance.

vocab.def: A minute-by-minute timeline of every activity, speaker, cue and staff assignment on event day.
A scheduling method that links dependent tasks to find the longest sequence that sets the minimum project duration.
The time between the decision to act and the date the action must be complete, such as booking a vendor before an event.
A pre-set alternative course of action to use if a planned element fails or a risk occurs.
The period when equipment, decor and vendors are brought into the venue before guests arrive.
A goal that is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.
The maximum number of people a room may legally hold, set by the local fire authority.
A scaled drawing showing where seating, stages, service areas and exits are placed in a venue.
A room layout with rows of chairs facing the front, used for presentations without dining.
A layout of round tables with chairs for guests to dine together.
A tentative reservation of a date and space that the venue keeps for a limited time before the client must sign.
A pre-event visit to confirm that the space, power, access and exits match the event plan.
A cost that stays the same regardless of attendance or sales volume, such as a venue rental fee.
A cost that changes with the number of guests or units, such as per-plate food cost.
The volume of attendance or sales at which total revenue equals total costs.
The difference between budgeted and actual amounts, labeled favorable or unfavorable.
Money set aside within a budget for unexpected costs.
A non-cash gift of goods or services, recorded at fair value.
A contract clause that excuses performance when extraordinary events beyond a party’s control prevent it.
A document issued by an insurer that confirms a vendor’s coverage limits and policy dates.
A partial payment made to secure a vendor’s services, with refund terms set by the contract.
A contract clause in which one party agrees to cover the other party’s losses from specified claims.
A document that asks vendors to submit detailed proposals for defined services so they can be compared.
A written document setting out the scope, price, dates and responsibilities of a vendor engagement.
The specific group an event or message is designed for and most likely to respond to it.
An explicit instruction telling the audience what to do next, such as register or buy a ticket.
The percentage of people who take a desired action, such as registering, out of those who saw the offer or visited the page.
A discounted ticket price offered for a limited period to encourage early commitment.
The number of times a piece of content is displayed, whether or not it is clicked or read.
A defined set of benefits, such as logo placement and mentions, offered to a sponsor for a set fee.
Any point at which a guest interacts with the event, such as registration, signage or a follow-up email.
The actions taken to restore a guest’s satisfaction after a service failure.
The overall impression a guest forms from every interaction before, during and after an event.
Design and service practices that let people with disabilities use facilities and attend events, required under the Americans with Disabilities Act for public accommodations.
A loyalty measure based on how likely guests are to recommend an experience, on a scale of 0 to 10.
A staff function that helps guests with requests, information and problems during an event or stay.
A stock rotation method in which the oldest inventory is used or sold first.
The temperature range of about 40 to 140 degrees F (4 to 60 degrees C) in which bacteria multiply rapidly, per USDA; the FDA Food Code uses 41 to 135 degrees F.
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points, a systematic food-safety method that identifies and controls hazards at critical points.
A guest or place setting charged for a meal, used as a unit of banquet pricing.
Food cost divided by menu price, expressed as a percentage, used to judge menu pricing.
A tested recipe with fixed ingredients, portions and method that allows consistent quality and cost per serving.
A process that identifies hazards, rates their likelihood and impact, and plans controls for each.
Coverage that pays for third-party bodily injury and property damage claims arising from the insured’s operations.
A signed document in which a participant acknowledges known risks and agrees to terms that may limit claims.
A written record of an injury, damage or unsafe condition, used for follow-up and insurance claims.
Permission to publicly play copyrighted music, typically obtained through an organization such as ASCAP, BMI or SESAC.
Failure to exercise the care a reasonable person would in the same situation, which can create liability when it causes harm.
A written statement of a role’s duties, responsibilities, time commitment and expectations.
A plan that assigns staff or volunteers to specific times and locations so coverage is clear.
Pay at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek by non-exempt employees.
Under the FLSA, an exempt employee is not eligible for overtime pay, and a non-exempt employee is eligible for it.
A situation in which a personal interest could improperly influence a professional decision, requiring disclosure and recusal.
A leadership style that gives clear instructions and close oversight, suited to new or inexperienced teams.
A structured meeting after an event to review results against goals and capture lessons learned.
Actual results divided by the goal, expressed as a percentage.
Total event cost divided by the number of attendees, used to measure spending efficiency.
The amount left after all costs are subtracted from gross revenue.
The number of survey responses divided by the number of people invited, used to judge how representative results are.
A review of the differences between budgeted and actual results to explain why they occurred.
